text:
Micah: Heads-up — after last night's toolkit rollout from CUDA 11.x -> 12.x, ~12% of gpu-nodes in us-west-2 are failing pod postStart hooks during container rebuilds. Symptoms: long cold-starts, ld.so errors, and a burst of NCCL timeouts.
Sara: any logs/snippets?
Micah: pasted one of the common failures below:
```
/usr/local/bin/python: error while loading shared libraries: libnvrtc-builtins.so.11: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/main.py", line 12, in <module>
    from torch._C import _init_names
ImportError: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.29' not found (required by /opt/cuda/lib64/libnvrtc.so)
```
Ajay: looks like runtime/host lib mismatch — images were built against the new toolkit headers but nodes still have older driver libs cached, or vice-versa. Also saw `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ld-2.31.so: undefined symbol: __gxx_personality_v0` in a few pods.
InfraBot: canary-rollout status: 2026-03-17T03:41Z -> 60% hosts patched; 15% failing health checks; auto-rollback disabled.
Nina: Are failures correlated to rebuilt containers only? Or also existing immutable images?
Micah: Mostly rebuilt images (we trigger a docker build in CI that picks up base-toolkit:latest). Old frozen images seem fine until a redeploy touches the CUDA libs.
Sara: repro steps? I can try on a spare node.
Ajay: quick repro: pull one of the failing images, run `ldd /opt/cuda/lib64/libnvrtc.so` and `gcc --version` inside the container and compare to host. Also check `modinfo nvidia` and `nvidia-smi` for kernel module vs driver version mismatch.
Micah: example host driver: 515.65; image expects 535.x. Also saw a metadata-loss case where PTX cache regen caused 2GB spike and OOM during first inference.
ops-sre: If PTX cache regen is the problem, we should avoid forcing full rebuild waves — that regen is very expensive and spikes cost. Suggest 1) drain + cordon a canary subset and repro, 2) add `--no-cache` only where necessary, 3) pin base-toolkit to a compat shim.
Nina: Agree on canary. Also need a short customer-facing note? Some high-traffic tenants saw latency spikes.
Micah: I'm drafting an ops note, will ping #support when we confirm rollback plan.
Sara: Workaround that helped one team: override LD_LIBRARY_PATH to point to runtime-compatible libs at container start, e.g., `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/cuda/compat/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` — not ideal but buys time.
Ajay: Long-term fix: we need image-building guidelines: 1) detect host driver version at deploy time, 2) avoid baking incompatible nvrtc/libstdc++ versions, or 3) ship a small runtime shim that maps to host libs. Also consider switching CI to `base-toolkit:12-compat` instead of `:latest`.
InfraBot: incident created: INC-2026-0317-47 (investigating).
ops-sre: Action items: Micah/Ajay to run canary repro (2 nodes), Nina to prepare tenant note if rollback needed, Sara to compile list of impacted images + digest, ops-sre to throttle rebuild pipeline. Target ETA for decision: 2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Micah: I'll start the canary now and post logs in this thread.
Sara: FYI — found an image that links against `libstdc++.so.6` from GCC 13, host has GCC 11 libs. That explains GLIBCXX symbols.
Ajay: If rollback chosen: we can pin cluster nodes to the older toolkit driver image and schedule controlled rebuilds for images that must move to 12.x.
Nina: Noted — also check NCCL config; some failures were `NCCL WARN CALL - internal cudaErrorLaunchFailure` during all-reduce after rebuilds. Could be kernel/driver pairing.
Micah: thanks all. Posting initial canary logs in ~10m. Please react with :thumbsup: if you can help validate.
